title: Prince Gong’s Mansion
representedDate: Standing post-conservation museum complex as documented by the 2014 exterior photography and museum guide.
geometryBasis: Named OpenStreetMap ways for ten halls, gates and garden structures, the garden and perimeter outlines, exact west pond and 60 supplementary Overture roofprints. Roofprints are fitted to discrete roofs with open courtyard space retained.
sectionBasis: Original Qualla photos establish low swept gray and glazed green roofs, carved tile ends, blue and green structural decoration, red columns, timber lattice and stone plinths. Official museum text establishes the two main precincts and landmarks. The museum identifies only the two main gates, Yin’an Hall and Jiale Hall as green glazed, with gray tiled wings and a two-story rear screen.
limitations: Individual heights, painted motifs and secondary roof shapes are interpreted. Supplemental roofprints locate roof cover rather than exact wall lines.
The Rear Building follows about 152 m of the mapped garden boundary. The overall 183 m length reported by the museum could not be located precisely from the available footprints.

The garden gate, theatre association and paths are approximated from mapped geometry and the museum’s written route. The pond water and pavilion terrace levels are fitted to the original elevation field and are approximate. Open ground and rockeries retain that field. Interiors are outside the model scope.
